To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stimulatory effects on SLα gene expression induced by SLα/SLα and IGF-I/IIF could be potentiated by TAC3/N3KR interactions in the carp pitutary.

the stimulatory effects induced by SLα/SLb and TAC3 gene product on SLα gene expression are further enhanced by the synergistic interactions between TAC3/Nk3r system and IGF-I/II signaling in the carp pitutary.
the potentiating effects on SLα autoregulation are mediated by the functional interactions between IGF-I/- II and TAC3 gene product in grass carp pitutary cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the molecular mechanism underlying the functional interactions between SLα/SLα and IGF-I-II/TAC3/NK2R in grass carp pitutary cells and the findings may provide a novel insight into the regulation of SLα gene expression at the pituitaty level.
a novel functional role of NK3R in the potentiating effect of SLα autoregulation in carp pituitary.

the novel functional roles of NK3R gene products in potentiating SLα autoregulation and these potentiatory actions of NK3R may be involved in the local control of SLα gene expression via up-regulation in the grass carp pituitaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the functional interactions between SLα/SLα, IGF-I/- II and TAC3 gene expression may play a critical role in the regulation of SLα gene expression at the pituitaries of grass carp, and this novel regulatory mechanism is likely to be mediated by up-regulation of the expression of NK3R.

NK3R expression may serve as an important regulatory target at the carp pituitaries and its expression could be up-regulated by SLα/SLß, IGF-I/-I and TAC3 gene product co-treatment and these stimulatory effects may be mediated via cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC and Ca2+ dependent cascades functionally linked to NK3R activation.
the TAC3/NKB/NK3/NK3/NKB/NKB/NK2R system may play a pivotal role in the regulation of SLα synthesis and release in the pituitary via the functional interactions with ICF-I/IGF-II and SLα.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NKB/NK1R and NKB/NK2R systems act at the pituaitary level to upregulate SLα synthesis, and that the NKB/SLα system can serve as a positive feedback loop to up-regulate NK3R expression in grass carp pitutary cells.

NKB/NK2R system may act at the pituaitary level to upregulate SLα synthesis via activation of NK3R in the carp pituaitary and NK3R activation may also be a regulatory target of other SLα regulators such as IGF-I/-IIs.

NKB and SLα/SLß are two independent stimulators of SLα synthesis and release in carp pituitary, but they could also act together to enhance the stimulatory effects on SLα synthesis via up-regulation in the expression of NK3R.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NK3R expression may play a critical role in the potentiating effects on SLα autoregulation in carp pituitary.

NK3R expression may serve as a regulatory signal at the pituitaries level to mediate SLα synthesis and release and that the potentiating effects of NK3R activation on SLα autoregulation may be mediated by IGF-I/-IIs.
NK3R expression may serve as a novel regulatory target for NKB and other pituitary factors in the regulation of SLα gene expression and secretion.
